subject.title: [BUG] exec tool: aborted run wedges subsequent exec calls in same session (regression from PR #94412)

question: Should this concrete v2026.6.11 exec/tool wedge be handled as a separate regression fix, or folded into the broader run-lifecycle reliability work in #101863?
rationale: Current source and production evidence prove the issue is still relevant, but the added macOS repro broadens the trigger beyond explicit exec abort and leaves the owner boundary ambiguous.

options.title: Require focused live repro first
options.body: Keep this issue open and require a current-main diagnostic that identifies whether exec process cleanup, active-tool diagnostics, or session-lane release owns the stale state before queueing a fix.

options.title: Fold into #101863 Track A/B
options.body: Treat this issue as covered by the lifecycle/liveness umbrella only if maintainers confirm that work explicitly releases or recovers the reported `tool:exec:started` blocked state.

options.title: Queue exploratory repair
options.body: Allow an automated attempt to add a focused regression test and narrow fix, accepting that it should stop if the root cause spans multiple lifecycle owners.

recommendation.title: Require focused live repro first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require a current-main diagnostic that identifies whether exec process cleanup, active-tool diagnostics, or session-lane release owns the stale state before queueing a fix.

likelyOwner.reason: vincentkoc merged and substantially shaped the abort-loop PR named as the regression source, making them the best initial router for separate fix versus umbrella folding.
